diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the second factor is a scalar and contains the orthogonal project $\mP\equiv \mi-\hat{\mc}_k^T\hat{\mc}_k^{\dagger}$, we can write it as

issues.failure_explanation: The Schur complement of the partitioned Gram matrix uses the projector \hat{\mc}_{k-1}\hat{\mc}_{k-1}^{\dagger} (an m×m matrix), not \hat{\mc}_k^T\hat{\mc}_k^{\dagger}, which is a product of a k×m and a k×m matrix and is dimensionally undefined. The projector \mP is consequently misdefined and the identity \det(vc^T vc − vc^T \hat{\mc}_k^T\hat{\mc}_k^{\dagger} vc) = ||\mP vc||^2 does not follow from the formula as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \hat{\mc}_k^T\hat{\mc}_k^{\dagger} by \hat{\mc}_{k-1}\hat{\mc}_{k-1}^{\dagger} in the Schur complement formula and in the definition of \mP.
issues.overall_effect: The Schur complement step in the induction proof of Theorem t_vol is invalid as written. After correcting the formula, the conclusion vol(\hat{\mc}_k) ≤ vol(\hat{\mc}_{k-1}) and the inapproximability threshold 2√2/3 follow.
issues.title: Dimensionally invalid Schur complement formula in volume bound proof
issues.why_classification: A single forced correction of the projector expression restores a standard Schur complement argument; the conclusion and guarantee are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is NP hard to approximate S-optimality maximization within a factor of $(2\sqrt{2}/3)^{1/k}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The gap reduction yields an inapproximability factor (2√2/3)^{1/k}, which converges to 1 as k→∞. Refuting a PTAS requires a constant gap bounded away from 1 independent of the input; a gap vanishing with k cannot distinguish true from false X3C instances for any fixed ε>0 and large k. The conclusion that no PTAS exists is not established.

failure_location.quote: Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for S-optimality maximization.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must supply a reduction producing a constant gap bounded away from 1 independently of k, or withdraw the no-PTAS claim.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that S-optimality maximization admits no PTAS is unsupported; the reduction only rules out approximation factors strictly below (2√2/3)^{1/k}, which depends on k.
issues.title: No-PTAS claim for S-optimality unsupported due to vanishing gap
issues.why_classification: Every supported resolution requires essentially new proof architecture (a constant-gap reduction) or causes major loss (withdrawal of the no-PTAS guarantee for a headline criterion).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We derive an inapproximability threshold of~$\sqrt{3/2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem statement gives the threshold 2/√3 ≈ 1.155, while the text and proof establish √(3/2) ≈ 1.225. These are different numerical values. The stated threshold understates the proved inapproximability.

failure_location.quote: It is NP hard to approximate two-norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse within a factor of $2/\sqrt{3}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change 2/√3 to √(3/2) in the theorem statement.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical inapproximability threshold for two-norm pseudo-inverse minimization is misstated in the theorem; the no-PTAS conclusion remains valid because the proved gap √(3/2) is a constant exceeding 1.
issues.title: Inconsistent inapproximability threshold in pseudo-inverse two-norm theorem
issues.why_classification: A one-number correction preserves every substantive claim and guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is NP hard to approximate Frobenius norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse within a factor of $\sqrt{1+\tfrac{1}{4k}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The inapproximability factor √(1+1/(4k)) converges to 1 as k→∞ because the additive gap of 1/4 in ‖C†‖_F² ≥ k+1/4 becomes negligible relative to the optimal value √k. The gap reduction cannot rule out a PTAS for large k. The same vanishing factor appears in t_pi3 and t_fcond.

failure_location.quote: Thus, unless P=NP, there is no PTAS for Frobenius norm minimization of the pseudo-inverse.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must produce a constant multiplicative gap bounded away from 1 independently of k, or withdraw the three no-PTAS claims.
issues.overall_effect: The no-PTAS claims for Frobenius pseudo-inverse minimization (t_pi), Schatten p pseudo-inverse minimization (t_pi3), and Frobenius condition number minimization (t_fcond) are all unsupported.
issues.title: No-PTAS claims for Frobenius and Schatten p pseudo-inverse unsupported due to vanishing gap
issues.why_classification: Every supported resolution requires new proof architecture or causes major loss (three advertised no-PTAS guarantees are withdrawn).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Hence, all singular values of $\mc$ are equal to 1, and $\mc$ has orthonormal columns.

issues.failure_explanation: From ∏_j σ_j/σ_1 = 1 the proof correctly deduces all singular values are equal (to σ_1), but then incorrectly concludes they equal 1. Equal singular values σ only imply the columns are orthogonal with common norm σ, not orthonormal. For example C = 2I_2 has rvol = 1 but non-unit column norms.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\rvol(\mc) = 1$  if and only if the columns of $\mc$ are orthonormal.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add the hypothesis ‖Ce_j‖_2 = 1 for 1 ≤ j ≤ k, or replace 'orthonormal' by 'orthogonal with equal column norms'.
issues.overall_effect: The general characterization of rvol(C) = 1 is wrong. Downstream uses in thm:rvolnp and t_volptas are unaffected because they assume unit-norm columns where orthogonal implies orthonormal.
issues.title: Wrong equality characterization in relative volume lemma
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the hypothesis or conclusion preserves all claims and dependents.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is a special case of the Schatten $p$-norm for $p=2$.

issues.failure_explanation: Since σ_1 ≥ 1 we have (k/σ_1^p)^{1/p} = k^{1/p}/σ_1 ≤ k^{1/p}, so the second inequality points the wrong way. The bound ‖C†‖_{(p)} ≥ k^{1/p} is not established. The Frobenius case (p = 2) inherits the same error because it is declared a special case of the same argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the Frobenius case directly via Cauchy–Schwarz ((∑σ_j²)(∑σ_j^{-2}) ≥ k²) and derive the Schatten p case via ‖C†‖_{(p)} ≥ k^{1/p-1/2}‖C†‖_F ≥ k^{1/p}.
issues.overall_effect: The optimal-value characterizations for Frobenius and Schatten p pseudo-inverse norms are unestablished, affecting NP-hardness (t_pi7) and no-PTAS (t_pi, t_pi3) results that use these optimal values.
issues.title: Reversed inequality in pseudo-inverse Schatten p-norm bound
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement argument using a standard norm inequality and Cauchy–Schwarz fixes the proof while preserving the lemma statement and all dependents.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The singular value ordering implies that all singular values are equal to~$1$, thus  $\mc$ has orthonormal columns.

issues.failure_explanation: The sums run to p instead of k (the matrix has k singular values). For k ≠ p the equations are wrong or ill-defined. Additionally, the argument only shows all singular values are equal to σ_k; concluding they equal 1 requires the additional step ∑σ_j² = k ⇒ σ_k = 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change p to k in both summation limits and add the step ∑σ_j² = k ⇒ σ_k = 1.
issues.overall_effect: The equality characterization for Schatten p mixed condition number is unestablished as written; the inequality direction is unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong summation bounds and incomplete argument in Schatten p mixed condition number case
issues.why_classification: Two short local corrections preserve every claim and guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The claim is false for p > 2. For C = I_4 partitioned into two 4×2 blocks (k = 2): ‖C†‖_{(p)}² = 4^{2/p} and ‖C_1†‖_{(p)}² + ‖C_2†‖_{(p)}² = 2·2^{2/p}. For p = 3 this gives 2.52 < 3.17, violating the inequality. The proof's error is the identity ‖diag(A,B)‖_{(q)} = ‖A‖_{(q)} + ‖B‖_{(q)}; the correct identity is ‖diag(A,B)‖_{(q)}^q = ‖A‖_{(q)}^q + ‖B‖_{(q)}^q.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the exponent 2 to p in the lemma statement (yielding the true inequality ‖C†‖_{(p)}^p ≥ ‖C_1†‖_{(p)}^p + ‖C_2†‖_{(p)}^p) and correct the block-diagonal norm identity in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The Schatten p-norm superadditivity inequality for partitioned pseudo-inverses is false as stated for p > 2.
issues.title: False Schatten p-norm superadditivity for partitioned pseudo-inverse
issues.why_classification: The claim is false and must be weakened (exponent 2 to p), but the corrected result is a recognizably comparable superadditivity statement proved by the same argument.
